messages:
Alex C: Putting up a short proposal — we need deterministic routing when both User-Agent and X-Auth-Context are present. Current gateway behavior prefers X-Auth-Context but that breaks some SDKs that don't set it. Proposal: introduce a precedence matrix + signed-header validation. Details below.
Mira L: yep, this is the pain. mobile SDKs send weird UAs and some proxies add X-Auth-Context for legacy customers. makes telemetry noisy.
Samir: Can we just canonicalize UA and extract sdk=redwood/<version> then use that as a tiebreaker?
Tzach: hmm canonicalization helps but spoofing risk. If UA indicates 'redwood-sdk' we should still verify an accompanying signature header or short-lived JWT.
Alex C: Agreed. Proposed rules: 1) If X-Redwood-Auth exists and is cryptographically signed -> authoritative tenant routing. 2) Else if UA matches official SDK pattern -> create ephemeral auth context with limited scope (no billing changes, no admin routes). 3) Else fallback to normal Authorization bearer token logic.
Mira L: +1 for scoped ephemeral auth. also ban it for admin/management routes.
Samir: Sketch of route config (pseudo-yaml):
```
routes:
  - match: headers["X-Redwood-Auth"].signed == true
    action: route_to_tenant(header("X-Tenant-ID"))
  - match: user_agent.matches("^redwood-sdk/[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+")
    action: route_to_sdk_pool(scope: "ephemeral", max_tokens_per_minute: 60)
  - match: header.present("Authorization")
    action: default_token_flow
```
Tzach: how do we surface this in Console? need telemetry flags to show when UA-derived routes used and a confidence score.
Alex C: We'll emit telemetry: routing.source = [signed_header|ua_inferred|token]; routing.auth_confidence = [high|medium|low]; and routing.affects_quota = true/false. These fields feed quota dashboards and alerting.
Mira L: Important: quota enforcement must use confidence. If low -> apply stricter rate limits and tighter caching. Also store raw headers for audit but redact after 30d.
Samir: Rollout plan: behind feature flag. Stage 0: enable for internal tenants and infra-only traffic for 3 days. Stage 1: 10% of production customers for 1 week. Monitor routing.source distribution, 401/403 delta, and cost delta.
deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: header-routing-ua-ephemeral v1 -> canary -> 2026-04-02T14:00Z
Alex C: I'll draft the PR w/ config + unit/integration tests. Also adding a small eval (prompt set) to ensure UA-derived routing doesn't change model selection or degrade quality.
Mira L: If anyone has edge cases (CDNs normalizing UA, corporate proxies injecting X-Auth-Context, or mobile webviews), drop them here so we can add tests.
Samir: one more constraint: UA-inferred tenant must never escalate to dedicated or non-isolated pools. No privilege escalation.
Tzach: noted. We'll enforce via routing.policy check that rejects scope-escalation. OK to proceed on the PR side.
